quotes.text:
kind-dependencies:
    - post-balrog-dummy
    - post-beetmover-dummy
    - release-balrog-submit-toplevel
    - release-update-verify-config
    - toolchain

transforms:
    - gecko_taskgraph.transforms.release:run_on_releases
    - gecko_taskgraph.transforms.release_deps:transforms
    - gecko_taskgraph.transforms.update_verify:transforms
    - gecko_taskgraph.transforms.job:transforms
    - gecko_taskgraph.transforms.task:transforms

task-defaults:
    run-on-repo-type: [hg]
    name: update-verify
    run-on-projects: []  # to make sure this never runs as part of CI
    shipping-phase: promote
    worker-type: b-linux

thunderbird-macosx64:
        description: macosx64 update verify
        shipping-product: thunderbird
        attributes:
            build_platform: macosx64-shippable
        fetches:
            toolchain:
                - linux64-libdmg

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The update-verify kind adds toolchain as a dependency and fetches linux64-libdmg for the macOS task. The current default worker is Linux and the task build_platform is macosx64-shippable. Keep execution host and verified target platform separate when selecting tools; the task name does not imply it runs on a macOS worker. No taskgraph generation or LZMA DMG validation ran here. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Fetch host tools for macOS update verification through the toolchain dependency
